name: Birmingham Civil Rights Institute
unique: A museum across from the 16th Street Baptist Church tracing the Birmingham movement, from the children's crusade to the bombing that killed four girls.
buzz: Powerful and specific, with the church across the street as part of the experience. Give it two hours.

name: Birmingham Museum of Art
unique: A free museum with a strong collection of American and European art, African masks, Asian ceramics and a sculpture garden.
buzz: Free and better than expected, with a good cafe. The African collection is the surprise.

name: Railroad Park
unique: A 19 acre linear park built along the railroad tracks downtown, with lawns, a skate park, a playground and a view of the viaducts.
buzz: The design turned a dead edge into the city's front yard. Good for a walk and a coffee.

name: McWane Science Center
unique: A hands on science center with a dinosaur hall, an aquarium, an IMAX and a bed of nails, in a former department store.
buzz: Good for kids of all ages, with enough to fill a rainy afternoon. The aquarium is smaller than it looks.

name: Rosa Parks Museum
unique: A museum at the site of the bus stop where Parks was arrested, with a reconstructed bus, original documents and a video of the boycott.
buzz: The bus and the archive are the strongest parts. Small enough for an hour and serious throughout.

name: Dexter Avenue King Memorial Baptist Church
unique: The church where Martin Luther King Jr. pastored during the Montgomery bus boycott, with the pulpit, the stained glass and a basement exhibit.
buzz: The sanctuary is still in use and the guides tell the boycott story from the pews. Dress respectfully.

name: The Legacy Museum
unique: A museum built on a former slave warehouse, tracing the line from slavery to mass incarceration with original testimony, art and data.
buzz: Heavy and essential, and the companion memorial nearby completes it. Give it time and go with someone.

name: Hank Williams Museum
unique: A collection of the country singer's suits, guitars, cars and handwritten lyrics, a few blocks from the stage where he started.
buzz: For fans it is a pilgrimage, and the 1952 Cadillac is the centerpiece. Small and earnest.

name: Bellingrath Gardens
unique: Sixty five acres of azaleas, camellias and roses on the Fowl River, with a 1930s mansion and a river cruise.
buzz: The spring azaleas are the show, and the house tour is a bonus. Hot in summer, so go early.

name: Mobile Carnival Museum
unique: A museum of Mardi Gras in the city that started it, with elaborate trains, crowns, robes and the story of the mystic societies.
buzz: The costumes are spectacular and the history explains why Mobile, not New Orleans, claims the first carnival.

name: Dauphin Street
unique: A downtown street of bars, restaurants and live music in historic buildings, with a Mardi Gras parade route running through it.
buzz: The bars are close together and the crowds are friendly. Busy on weekends and during carnival.

name: US Space and Rocket Center
unique: A museum with a Saturn V rocket overhead, a space shuttle, simulators and the original Space Camp, on the arsenal road.
buzz: The Saturn V hall is awe inspiring and the simulators are fun for kids. Allow half a day.

name: Monte Sano State Park
unique: A CCC park on a mountain above Huntsville with trails, a lodge, cabins and overlooks of the Tennessee Valley.
buzz: The trails are well built and the overlooks are the payoff. Less crowded than the space center.

name: Moundville Archaeological Park
unique: A Mississippian mound complex with 29 mounds, a plaza and a museum of engraved pottery and copper, on the Black Warrior River.
buzz: The scale is impressive and the museum explains the culture well. Climb the big mound for the view.

name: Paul W. Bryant Museum
unique: A museum of Alabama football with championship trophies, game film and the story of Bear Bryant, on the campus.
buzz: Even non fans get pulled into the history. Game weekends are packed.

name: DeSoto Falls
unique: A 104 foot waterfall in a stone gorge on Lookout Mountain, with a short trail and a swimming area below.
buzz: The falls are easy to reach and the pool is cold. A good stop on the way to Little River Canyon.

name: Little River Canyon
unique: A 600 foot deep canyon on Lookout Mountain with a rim drive, waterfalls and trails, one of the deepest canyons east of the Mississippi.
buzz: The rim drive has the overlooks and the canyon floor has the waterfalls. Go after rain for the flow.

name: Noccalula Falls
unique: A 90 foot waterfall in a city park with a gorge trail, a miniature train, a campground and a statue of the Cherokee woman the falls are named for.
buzz: The gorge trail gets you behind the falls, which kids love. The park is old fashioned and cheap.

name: Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art
unique: A university museum with American and European art, a sculpture garden and a cafe, free to the public.
buzz: Small and free, with good temporary shows. A quiet break from campus.

name: Edmund Pettus Bridge
unique: The bridge where marchers were beaten on Bloody Sunday in 1965, now a National Historic Landmark with a view of the Alabama River.
buzz: Walking across is the experience, and the interpretive center nearby explains the march. Quiet and heavy.

name: Old Courthouse Museum
unique: A courthouse museum in the town that shaped Harper Lee and Truman Capote, with a courtroom modeled on the one in To Kill a Mockingbird.
buzz: For readers it is a pilgrimage, and the annual play is performed in the courtroom. Check the schedule.
